study type: Secondary data analysis of nationally representative household surveys
exposure: Type of healthcare facility (private vs. public)
outcome: Proportion of deliveries by caesarean section
cohort: Women aged 15-49 years with a live birth in the two years preceding the survey in nine Arab countries in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA)
finding: Caesarean section use varied widely across the MENA region and was more common among the richest quintiles and in private healthcare facilities.
mod_finding: Cesarean section use was higher in private sector facilities compared to public sector facilities.
country: Nine Arab countries in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA)
